name: Tempester n°16: SysEx rings moved out of the undo beat (beat 16) in the external SRAM
explanation: The external SRAM (PMP, 16-bit data, CS = RA6, 18-bit word address: PMADDR + RA0/RA1) holds the events of beat 16 (the Revert/Compare/undo copy of the current beat, [routine](x,0x10) and [routine](x,0x10)) at words 0x3AA00-0x3D9FF. The received-SysEx ring (0x4000 bytes, 2 per word) sat at words 0x3C000-0x3DFFF: every received SysEx byte (DIN or USB, written from ring index 0 after each F0) overwrote beat 16 from step 176 on, and a copy into beat 16 during a SysEx reception overwrote the bytes not yet parsed. Both use the same word addresses through the same primitives ([routine] / [routine]), so the overlap is physical. Fix: the received ring moves to words 0x3E000-0x3FFFF (same size, same indexing, index & 0x3fff), and the send ring (0x800 bytes, DIN only), which used 0x3E000-0x3E3FF, moves to 0x3DC00-0x3DFFF. 0x3DA00-0x3FFFF is reached by no other code: the only SRAM chip-select sites are the four primitives, [routine], [routine], [routine], [routine] and [routine] (instruction scan), and their non-ring users address sounds (< 0xAA00) or events of beats 0-16 (< 0x3DA00); the OS updates write the image from word 0 (Main: the whole SRAM, then never return) and are unaffected. Four immediates changed in place, no code added. Beat 16 keeps whatever a previous SysEx left in it until the next beat selection or recording.
